title: JoyLink: Phone as Gamepad
shortDescription: Bluetooth game controller, touchpad & TV remote for PC, Mac & Android TV
tagline: Turn your phone into a real Bluetooth gamepad — no receiver app, no dongle, no root

sections.title: Turn your phone into a real Bluetooth gamepad — no receiver app, no dongle, no root
paragraphs: JoyLink makes your Android phone show up as a standard Bluetooth game controller, touchpad and TV remote. Pair it once with a Windows PC, Mac, Linux machine, Android TV or another Android phone and it works like any wireless gamepad — nothing to install on the other side.

sections.title: Popular ways people use JoyLink
bullets: Play emulators and Steam games on a laptop that has no controller
Navigate Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV and type with your phone keyboard
Couch gaming: control the PC from the sofa
Retro gaming on a Raspberry Pi or RetroPie without buying a pad
Two phones, two players on one computer

sections.title: Bluetooth Gamepad for PC, Mac & Linux
bullets: Xbox-style layout: dual analog sticks, D-pad, A B X Y, LB/RB, LT/RT, Start and Select
Standard (DirectInput) controller for Steam, emulators and any game that supports generic pads; Steam Input covers XInput-only titles
Haptic feedback, full-screen landscape, hold-to-exit so nothing kicks you out mid-game
Built-in button tester shows what each control sends to the host

sections.title: Touchpad, Mouse & Keyboard
bullets: Tap, two-finger scroll, right click and drag gestures
Type with your phone keyboard — ideal for TV boxes and media PCs
Works as a wireless mouse and keyboard for iPad and iPhone too

sections.title: TV Remote for Android TV, Google TV & Fire TV
bullets: D-pad navigation, Back, Home, Menu and power off
Volume, mute, play/pause, skip and channel up/down
Number pad and a text panel for search boxes

sections.title: Custom Layouts, Turbo & Macros
bullets: Move, resize and fade every control; up to 8 layouts for different games
Turbo (rapid fire) on any button; record a combo once, replay it from one macro key

sections.title: Racing Wheel for PC, TV & Emulators: Tilt to Steer
bullets: Hold the phone sideways and tilt to steer — for hosts whose screen can't tilt
Pedals on LT/RT out of the box; analog, left-stick and retro presets for sims and emulators

sections.title: Three complete themes
paragraphs: HUD (electric lime esports), Aurora (glass and cyan glow) and Industrial (keycaps and safety orange) — full looks, not just an accent colour.

sections.title: Built for long sessions
bullets: Lag in the same range as a regular Bluetooth controller
Auto reconnect when the host drops the link, keep screen on while you play
19 languages and a built-in FAQ

sections.title: Free forever, Pro is a one-time purchase
paragraphs: Connecting, pairing and the standard gamepad are free — no time limit, no ads. Pro adds touchpad, TV remote, racing wheel, custom layouts, turbo & macros and two extra themes for a single one-time price, not a subscription. Try each Pro feature once before you buy.

sections.title: Privacy first
paragraphs: JoyLink only asks for the Nearby devices (Bluetooth) permission plus a status notification. No account, no sign-in; your inputs go over Bluetooth to the host and nowhere else.

sections.title: Before you install
paragraphs: Something not working? A Play review gives us no way to ask for details or send a fix. Email feedback@dapplebyte.com instead (Settings → About → Send feedback attaches your phone model and app version) and we'll get back to you.
bullets: PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo Switch only accept their own controllers, so JoyLink can't connect to consoles
iOS games don't read generic Bluetooth gamepads, so on iPhone and iPad JoyLink is a mouse and keyboard only
Android can act as a Bluetooth gamepad, but some phone makers switch it off in firmware and no app can turn it back on; JoyLink checks on first launch
Every host maps buttons its own way; the button tester and FAQ cover the common cases
The racing wheel is for PC, TV boxes and emulators: most mobile racing games don't take controllers, and the phone you play on already has tilt steering of its own
